The Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) stated that statements have been taken in relation to the case. The dog involved is currently under observation at an animal management centre under the department's jurisdiction.

The AFCD stated that on July 10, the dog involved had been detained in connection with another case of biting another dog. When the owner retrieved the dog, the AFCD had warned that the dog must be securely leashed with a leash not exceeding two metres in length in public places, and properly controlled, so as not to cause nuisance or harm to other people or animals.

The owner of the deceased Bichon Frise named Weewei posted a tribute on social media today. The owner said that Weewei enjoyed going out and went for walks twice a day. Yesterday, while walking in the pet park, a dog about half a person's height suddenly rushed out and bit Weewei on the neck.

The owner recalled trying various methods, including kicking the large dog, spraying water at its nose, and using treats to distract it, but the large dog held on tightly and would not release Weewei. The owner said: "I screamed for help and am grateful to the kind passers-by who assisted, but faced with a large dog weighing several dozen pounds that would not let go, there was nothing anyone could do. I could only watch helplessly as my little dog lost her life."

Weewei died on the spot. The owner recalled that the large dog remained guarding Weewei's body until police arrived and restrained it, after which the owner was able to collect the remains. "I later learned that the vicious dog had also killed another small dog. From start to finish, the owner of the large dog never appeared."

The owner said the family was deeply grieved by the sudden tragedy and had been unable to sleep all night. "Weewei was an especially well-behaved and gentle little dog, the little angel of our entire family. I long to hold her again and kiss her. I cannot believe she has suddenly left us like this." The owner uploaded the last video of Weewei before the incident, showing her sitting in a stroller in a shopping mall, looking well-behaved and adorable. The owner said: "Only by repeatedly watching her curious and adorable appearance can I temporarily forget the horrifying scene."

The AFCD pointed out that, under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, large dogs weighing 20 kilogrammes or above must be securely leashed with a leash not exceeding two metres in length in public places. Offenders are liable to a fine of HK$25,000 and imprisonment for three months.

Under Section 23 of the Rabies Ordinance, dogs must be leashed or otherwise properly controlled when in a public place, or elsewhere where it could reasonably be expected that the dog would roam into a public place. Offenders are liable to a fine of HK$10,000.

Furthermore, under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Ordinance, any person who cruelly or unreasonably causes or fails to cause any act resulting in any animal suffering any unnecessary pain commits an offence and is liable upon conviction to a maximum fine of HK$200,000 and imprisonment for three years.
